# Development Log - 2026-06-21

Source: https://github.com/kcsujeet/ilamy-calendar/blob/main/docs/logs/2026-06-21.md

# Development Log - 2026-06-21

## Changes

- **[skill]**: Extended the code-review skill's DRY coverage (`.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`) to flag re-implementation of existing code, not just within-diff repetition. New section-D checklist item "Reuse of existing code checked": for every new function/component/hook/type/constant the diff adds, grep the codebase (shared packages first: `@ilamy/ui`, `@ilamy/utils`, `@ilamy/types`; then `lib/`/`utils/`/`hooks/`/adjacent files) for an existing equivalent and flag the duplicate with the name/path to reuse. Grep recipe: by name fragments AND by signature/shape. The section-D intro now frames DRY as two directions (reuse what exists + extract repetition).

- **[drag-to-create / Phase 1]**: Self-describing cells — the only core change for the drag-to-create feature (`docs/drag-to-create-plan.md`, issue #209). `DroppableCell` now exposes its existing `CellInfo`/slot range as DOM data attributes: `data-start`/`data-end` (ISO, from `getCellRange`), `data-resource-id` (when the cell has a `resourceId`), `data-all-day` (`"true"` only on all-day cells). Generic, no logic; lets the plugin hit-test the grid and rebuild a `CellInfo` from the DOM without core exposing any selection concept. TDD: 7 tests added to `droppable-cell.test.tsx` (red → green).

- **[drag-to-create / Phase 2]**: New plugin package `@ilamy/calendar-drag-to-create` (`packages/plugins/drag-to-create`), bundled into `@ilamy/calendar` and exposed at the `@ilamy/calendar/plugins/drag-to-create` subpath (same scaffolding as agenda/recurrence: package.json, bunup, tsconfig, test infra; calendar wiring in bunup entry/noExternal, package.json exports + devDep, tsconfig path, root build script). `dragToCreatePlugin({ onSelect? })` registers a `provider` that owns the whole gesture: pointer tracking on the calendar root (primary button only, single `pointerId`, cleanup on pointercancel/lostpointercapture/blur/Escape), a click-vs-drag distance threshold (matches @dnd-kit's `distance: 2`), single-region clamp (never mixes all-day/timed, one resource, full-day cells — month day-cells + the all-day row — span days while sub-day timed slots clamp to the start day), a `pointer-events:none` mirror portal positioned from the cells' rects, trailing-click suppression so `onCellClick` doesn't double-fire, and reverse-drag normalization. Default `onSelect` opens the event form preselected with `{ start, end, allDay, resourceId }`; a custom `onSelect(cellInfo, { openEventForm })` replaces it. Selection payload reuses the public `CellInfo`. The DOM-heavy logic is split into pure, unit-tested utils (`read-cell`, `selection`); 18 tests in the package.

- **[drag-to-create / fix]**: Timezone round-trip bug — dragging Jun 1→29 in America/Halifax created an event ending Jun 30 (form showed 3:00 AM / 2:59 AM, the UTC wall-clock). Root cause (proven empirically against the configured dayjs, not assumed): `data-start`/`data-end` are UTC ISO (`toISOString()`), and `@ilamy/utils/dayjs` aliases the `dayjs()` constructor to `dayjs.tz()` (see `dayjs.ts:84`). Under the calendar's `dayjs.tz.setDefault(timezone)` (set in `use-calendar-engine.ts:196`), `dayjs.tz('…T03:00:00Z', tz)` reads the **literal** `03:00` wall-clock and stamps it as `tz` instead of converting the instant — so a 00:00-Halifax cell round-tripped back to 03:00. An interim fix using `dayjs(iso).tz(timezone)` did NOT help (the constructor mis-parse happens before `.tz()`). Correct fix: parse the instant explicitly with `dayjs.utc(iso)`, then `.tz(timezone)` (or `.local()` when no calendar tz). The normal cell-click path is unaffected because it reuses the cell's original Dayjs and never serializes→reconstructs through a `Z` string. The same fix corrects the `isSameRegion` same-day clamp (was comparing the wrong day) and the form's End Date display (the form derives both date and time from this Dayjs; the `toDate()`→`dayjs(jsDate)` path has no Z-string mis-parse). Verified via a node probe across `TZ=America/Halifax` and `TZ=UTC`. The unit test was falsely green because it never called `setDefault`; it now does, reproducing the bug (RED) before the fix (GREEN).
  - Process note: a long detour chased "stale code" in the demo. Real cause was a `bun dev`→child-`vite` orphan holding `:4100` with `strictPort: true`, so restarts silently failed and the browser kept serving old modules. Diagnosis is environment-level (kill by port, not by the `bun dev` pid); the feature code was never the problem there.
- **[demo]**: Registered `dragToCreatePlugin()` in `@ilamy/playground`'s `createDemoPlugins` so the live demo/website exercise the feature (the pointer drag is not unit-testable in happy-dom; this is the manual-verification path).
- **[drag-to-create / specs]**: Expanded `read-cell.test.ts` tz coverage into a `timezone reconstruction` describe block: UTC-behind zone (Halifax, the reported bug), UTC-ahead zone (Tokyo, ISO date precedes local date), and the no-timezone instant-preservation case. Added a `withCalendarTimezone(tz, run)` helper that calls `dayjs.tz.setDefault` so the tests reproduce the app (the prior single test was falsely green without it). 24 tests in the package.
- **[drag-to-create / fix]**: Two mirror-overlay bugs found in the demo (short "Extra Small 300px" calendar). (1) The selection overlay painted far outside the calendar body: the mirror was the union of the start/last cell `getBoundingClientRect()`s, which extend past the clipped (scrolled) calendar body, and the overlay is portaled to `document.body` so the body's overflow can't clip it. Fix: clip the mirror to the `[data-testid="calendar-body"]` ancestor rect. Extracted pure `unionRect(Rect, Rect)` (moved off the old element-based version) and new `intersectRect(Rect, Rect): Rect | null` into `selection.ts`; the provider's `computeMirror` reads the DOMRects and clips. 7 new pure specs in `selection.test.ts` (incl. the exact overflow case, full-edge clip, and zero-area edge-touch → null). (2) Native text selection highlighted event titles/day-numbers during a drag. Fix: on gesture activation, set `user-select: none` (+ `-webkit-user-select`) on `document.body` and clear any in-progress selection; restored in `reset()` (covers commit/cancel/blur/Escape). 31 tests in the package. Note: clipping couples to the existing `data-testid="calendar-body"` marker (the visible calendar bounds for both regular and resource calendars).
- **[drag-to-create / core fix]**: Feature didn't work in vertical daily-granularity views (resource month vertical, week at daily granularity). Root cause: `vertical-grid-col.tsx` passed `hour={day.hour()}` for ALL cells, so even a `gridType="day"` cell described a 00:00-01:00 one-hour range instead of a full day. That made `isFullDaySpan` false, so the plugin's cross-day clamp rejected every other cell and the selection never extended. The horizontal grid already does `hour={gridType === 'hour' ? day.hour() : undefined}` (which is why month worked). Fix: mirror that conditional in `vertical-grid-col.tsx` so daily cells emit a full-day range. Side benefit: click-create on a daily vertical cell now makes a full-day event (consistent with horizontal month) instead of a midnight 1-hour event. TDD: new `vertical-grid-col.test.tsx` case asserts a `gridType="day"` cell's `data-end - data-start` is 23h (RED before, GREEN after); also set the test helper's default `gridType: 'hour'` so the existing hourly/sub-hour tests still exercise hourly behavior. Full calendar suite 795 pass.
- **[drag-to-create / review fixes]**: Code-review cleanup. Removed two leftover debug `console.log`s from the demo-debugging session (`use-calendar-navigation.ts`, `droppable-cell.tsx` — both ran on every render). Replaced the mirror-clip's `[data-testid="calendar-body"]` selector with a stable semantic marker: added `data-calendar-viewport="true"` to the calendar body in `ilamy-calendar.tsx` (test id kept) and pointed `computeMirror` at `[data-calendar-viewport]`, so a test-id rename can't silently break the overlay clipping. Fixed a stale `dragcreate` → `drag-to-create` comment in the plugin's `bunup.config.ts`. Calendar 795 + plugin 31 tests pass; type-check + biome clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `noConsole`-suppression warning left as-is).
- **[drag-to-create / refactor review]**: Post-review cleanup of PR #214. (1) Removed the unused public `DragSelection` export from the plugin index, it's the internal return of `computeRange` and no public signature used it (siblings only export consumer-facing types). (2) Split the mirror rect geometry (`Rect`/`unionRect`/`intersectRect`) out of `selection.ts` into `utils/rect.ts` + `rect.test.ts`, so `selection.ts` is just selection semantics and the layout matches the agenda plugin's one-concern-per-util-file convention. (3) Dropped the one-field `DragToCreateContext` wrapper; `onSelect` now takes `(selection, openEventForm)` directly. 31 plugin tests pass (now across 4 files); calendar + plugin type-check and biome clean.
- **[drag-to-create / contract tests]**: Closed a silent-failure gap. The plugin depends on an implicit cross-package DOM contract that no test covered: removing it would break the plugin with nothing failing. Added two tests in `ilamy-calendar.test.tsx`: (1) the calendar body carries `data-calendar-viewport` (the overlay clips to it — verified the test goes red when the marker is stripped, green when restored), (2) a rendered calendar emits cells with `data-start`/`data-end` end-to-end (catches a view refactor that stops rendering `DroppableCell`, which the isolated `droppable-cell.test` would miss). Swept every attribute the plugin reads (`data-start/end/resource-id/all-day/disabled`, `data-calendar-viewport`) against producer-side tests; the viewport marker was the only fully-uncovered one. Calendar suite 797.
- **[drag-to-create / readability]**: Extracted the selection-mirror `createPortal` out of an unreadable multi-line ternary into a named `SelectionMirror` component; the provider return is now `{mirror && <SelectionMirror rect={mirror} />}`. (Review miss: the multi-line-ternary sweep had flagged it, but it was wrongly triaged as idiomatic-React and dropped.)
- **[drag-to-create / mobile touch]**: Touch support. Researched custom-vs-library for unified mouse+touch (registry + MDN grounded); kept custom, no library fits a calendar-cell range-select in a published plugin (@dnd-kit is item→droppable, wrong model; @use-gesture 37KB, last-published 2024, still needs manual `touch-action`; selecto 910KB + 10 transitive deps + element-lasso model). Root cause of "not working on mobile": the browser claims a touch press-drag for scrolling and fires `pointercancel` → our reset (per MDN `touch-action`). Implemented the chosen long-press UX: touch press-and-hold (`LONG_PRESS_MS` 400ms, abort if it moves past `TOUCH_CANCEL_SLOP_PX` 10px first) enters select mode then drag selects; a quick swipe still scrolls; mouse/pen keep the 2px threshold. On activation a non-passive `touchmove` `preventDefault` suppresses scroll for the rest of the gesture (`setPointerCapture` not needed — listeners are global on `window`); reused `exceedsThreshold` for the cancel slop. Touch path is integration-level (not unit-testable in happy-dom: no `elementFromPoint`/`getBoundingClientRect`/timers); pure pieces (threshold/region/range/rect) stay covered. Needs real-device verification.
- **[drag-to-create / refactor]**: Broke the provider apart along a generic-vs-domain seam (not mouse-vs-touch, which would re-introduce parallel input paths). New `hooks/use-drag-gesture.ts`: a domain-agnostic, Pointer-Events press-drag recognizer `useDragGesture<T>({ resolvePress, onStart, onMove, onEnd, onCancel, thresholdPx?, longPressMs?, touchCancelSlopPx? })`. It owns ALL the input mechanics (mouse/pen threshold vs touch long-press, touch scroll suppression, text-selection lock, trailing-click suppression, the latest-callbacks ref, listener wiring + cleanup) with no calendar knowledge. The provider shrank ~291→122 lines and now holds only calendar logic: resolve a cell from a press, extend to the cell under the pointer within the same region, commit the range, render the mirror. `computeMirror` now takes `(startCell, lastCell)` instead of a Gesture; the manual `latest` ref is gone (internalized by the hook). Behavior-preserving (type-check + 31 tests + biome clean). Hook is plugin-internal for now (one consumer); promote to a shared package if a second one appears.
- **[drag-to-create / hook tests]**: Extracting `useDragGesture` made the gesture state machine unit-testable (it no longer touches `elementFromPoint`/`getBoundingClientRect` — those stayed in the provider's callbacks). Added `use-drag-gesture.test.ts` (15 tests) driving the hook with synthetic `PointerEvent`s via `renderHook`: mouse start/move/end, tap fires nothing, sub-threshold no-start, null-press ignored, custom `thresholdPx`, non-primary button ignored; Escape / pointercancel / blur cancel; touch long-press start→track→end, swipe-before-hold aborts, sub-slop jitter doesn't; user-select lock/unlock, trailing-click suppressed once; unmount removes listeners. Verified happy-dom carries PointerEvent init fields and bun:test has no fake timers, so the touch tests pass `longPressMs: 1` + a ~20ms real delay (the hook's configurable durations made this clean). Also added an `unlockTextSelection()` to the hook's unmount cleanup (restores body style if unmounted mid-drag). 46 plugin tests total.
- **[drag-to-create / docs]**: Corrected the stale "week/day views" scope in comments/docs — the feature works in month, week, and day views, regular and resource calendars, both orientations. Updated the plugin's `dragToCreatePlugin` doc comment (added the mouse-threshold vs touch-press-and-hold note), the `createDemoPlugins` comment, and `docs/drag-to-create-plan.md` (Status → Shipped (PR #214) with final scope, the `useDragGesture` hook, and the real-device-vs-Chrome-responsive-emulation caveat for touch).
- **[drag-to-create / feature]**: Edge auto-scroll during drag. When the pointer reaches a scroll-container edge, the container now scrolls per animation frame and the selection extends to the cell that scrolls under the (stationary) pointer, so you can select past the visible area in every view, including horizontal/vertical resource calendars (both axes). Implemented in `useDragGesture` (DRY: any drag gets it): on pointerdown it finds the cell's nearest scrollable ancestor; on each active move it tracks the last pointer point and runs an rAF loop that `scrollBy`s (forced `behavior: 'instant'`) and re-fires `onMove` while near an edge, self-stopping otherwise; torn down on end/cancel/unmount. The per-axis decision is the pure, unit-tested `computeEdgeScroll(point, rect, {edge, speed})` in `rect.ts` (6 specs: each edge, center no-op, corner both-axes). The rAF/scroll wiring isn't happy-dom-testable (no layout), so it's covered by the pure helper + manual verification; the 15 existing hook tests still pass (auto-scroll no-ops without a scroll container). 53 plugin tests. Follow-on fix surfaced by auto-scroll: when the start cell scrolled above the viewport, the mirror painted over the sticky header / all-day row (it clipped to `[data-calendar-viewport]`, the whole calendar body). Now `computeMirror` clips to the grid's actual scroll container (top below the header/all-day), falling back to the viewport marker when nothing scrolls. The scroll-container lookup is now one shared `findScrollContainer` (`utils/scroll.ts`) used by both the hook (auto-scroll target) and the mirror clip (DRY).
- **[drag-to-create / feature]**: Enabled cross-day timed selection (week/day hourly). Dragging from a timed cell into another day now selects a multi-day timed range instead of clamping to the start day. The change was just simplifying `isSameRegion` to its essential clamps (`sameAllDay && sameResource`), which removed the now-dead `isFullDaySpan`/`FULL_DAY_HOURS`; `computeRange` already produced the correct `first.start → last.end` span. Verified the core time grid already renders multi-day timed events as per-day clamped segments (`vertical.ts` `getEventPosition` clamps start-before-day → top 0 and end-after-day → bottom, and each column queries overlapping events), so the committed event displays correctly. TDD: flipped the `isSameRegion` "different day" spec to expect allowed (RED → GREEN) and added a cross-day `computeRange` case; 47 plugin tests. YAGNI: kept the bounding-box mirror (precise for the common same-day drag, approximate across days); a per-column staircase mirror stays deferred (plan §8).
- **[test / DRY]**: Consolidated `droppable-cell.test.tsx` to a single module-level `renderCell(opts)` helper (one `RenderCellOptions` covering the calendar/cell props each block varies), replacing four near-identical setups (`renderDroppableCellWithView` + three local `renderCell`s) and one inline render. Standardized the cell testid to `"cell"`. 21 tests unchanged/pass; file 325→258 lines.
- **[test / fix]**: Restored the `describe('DroppableCell getCellClassName')` block (3 tests) in `droppable-cell.test.tsx`, dropped during the `main` merge conflict (this branch and #211 both added describe blocks to the same file). Recovered verbatim from `origin/main`; the existing imports/`initialDate` already covered it. Full calendar suite 808.
- **[docs / decision]**: Considered widening `translations?: Translations` to `Partial<Translations>` (so adding keys isn't a breaking change), then reverted: for a localization API the full type is the safer contract (it forces every key, so a missing one is a compile error, not a silently-English label), and key-additions being a minor break is by design. Partial overrides are served by spreading the exported `defaultTranslations`. Captured the rationale in `docs/translation-usage.md` ("Why `translations` requires every key") so it isn't re-attempted.
- **[docs / findings]**: Documented the configured-dayjs zone-carrying-string bug in `docs/configured-dayjs-timezone-bug.md` — root cause (the `dayjs()`→`dayjs.tz()` alias + how `dayjs.tz` re-stamps a string's literal digits as the target tz, per the plugin source), the safe `dayjs.utc(iso).tz(tz)` pattern, and the verified library-wide affected-site list (consumer event ingestion in `normalize.ts:40-41`; recurrence `update-recurring-event.ts:69/256` and `ical.ts` EXDATE/RECURRENCE-ID; `generate-recurring-events.ts` until). Confirmed it's an **upstream dayjs bug** (iamkun/dayjs#2946, open; proposed PR #2949) that our wrapper inherits library-wide; the upstream workaround `dayjs(str).tz(tz)` doesn't work for us because our `dayjs()` is already `dayjs.tz()`. **Decision: the library-wide fix is a separate effort, not part of this PR** — drag-to-create works around it locally via `read-cell`'s `dayjs.utc().tz()`. The demo/tests build event dates as Dayjs/Date so the consumer-ingestion path isn't exercised today, but the public `start: Dayjs | Date | string` contract leaves it exposed.

- `packages/calendar/src/components/droppable-cell.test.tsx` - New "self-describing attributes (drag-create)" describe block (7 tests).

## Notes

- Verified: full `bun run build` (all packages + demo + website 24 pages), `type-check` all workspaces, full test suite (drag-to-create 18, agenda 19, recurrence 165, calendar 794), biome, and the Fallow gate — all green.
- Works in every view/orientation with no geometry-specific code: month + regular week/day + resource calendars (vertical columns and horizontal rows) all fall out of the attribute-based region rule (`isFullDaySpan` from the cell's range duration + the `data-resource-id` clamp). Month/all-day selections span days; timed slots clamp to the start day; a drag stays within one resource regardless of orientation.
- happy-dom can't exercise the real pointer drag (`elementFromPoint`/`getBoundingClientRect`), so the drag *logic* is covered by pure-util tests and the actual gesture is verified manually via the demo. Auto-scroll-at-edges, the in-grid mirror slot, and a precise per-cell month mirror are deferred per the plan (MVP uses a body-portal bounding-box mirror recomputed on pointermove); cross-day *timed* ranges also stay deferred.
- Deleted `docs/logs/2026-06-06.md` to stay under the 10-file cap.

# Development Log - 2026-06-22

Source: https://github.com/kcsujeet/ilamy-calendar/blob/main/docs/logs/2026-06-22.md

# Development Log - 2026-06-22

## Changes

- **[drag-to-create]**: Orientation-aware edge auto-scroll. The gesture hook now
  takes a `scrollAxis` (`'x' | 'y' | 'both'`) and zeroes the off-axis scroll
  delta, so a horizontal resource grid can't auto-scroll vertically across
  resources (and vice versa). The provider derives it: `'both'` for regular
  calendars, and the resource layout axis (`vertical -> 'y'`, else `'x'`) when
  resources are present.
- **[drag-to-create]**: Selection mirror now renders *inside* the grid's scroll
  content instead of as a body-portal overlay. It mounts into the new
  `data-calendar-scroll-content` box (positioned `absolute`, `z-15`), so it
  scrolls with the cells, is clipped by the scroll viewport, and is painted
  beneath the sticky header (`z-21`) and resource column (`z-20`). This fixes the
  overlay covering the resource-calendar header/columns. Falls back to the
  previous body-fixed overlay (clipped to `data-calendar-viewport`) when no
  scroll content is found.
- **[calendar]**: Exposed the resolved `orientation` (`'horizontal' | 'vertical'`)
  on the public `IlamyCalendarApi` so plugins can read the layout axis through
  the public context rather than reaching into internals.
- **[calendar]**: Added `data-calendar-scroll-content` (and `relative`) to the
  vertical/horizontal grid scroll-content boxes as a stable plugin mount contract
  (mirrors the existing `data-calendar-viewport` precedent).
- **[calendar]**: Narrowed `CalendarContextType.getCellClassName` from
  `(info) => string | undefined` to `=> string`, matching the sibling
  declarations (`provider.tsx`, `types/index.ts`, public `dist`) and
  `isCellDisabled`. Pure type consistency: the value flows into `cn()` via an
  optional call, so the empty case was already dropped. No behavior change.

## Files Modified

- `packages/plugins/drag-to-create/src/hooks/use-drag-gesture.ts` - `scrollAxis`
  option + per-axis gating of the auto-scroll delta.
- `packages/plugins/drag-to-create/src/components/drag-to-create-provider.tsx` -
  `computeMirror`/`SelectionMirror` reworked to mount inside the scroll content;
  derives and passes `scrollAxis`.
- `packages/plugins/drag-to-create/src/utils/scroll.ts` - doc comment updated
  (mirror no longer clips to the scroll container).
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/hooks/use-smart-calendar-context.ts` -
  added `orientation` to `IlamyCalendarApi` and the public hook.
- `packages/calendar/src/components/vertical-grid/vertical-grid.tsx`,
  `packages/calendar/src/components/horizontal-grid/horizontal-grid.tsx` - added
  `data-calendar-scroll-content` + `relative` to the scroll-content box.
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/ilamy-calendar.test.tsx` -
  tests asserting the public context exposes `orientation` (resolved + default).

## Review follow-ups (PR #214)

- **[drag-to-create]**: Removed the duplicate `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_PX` constant from
  `use-drag-gesture.ts`; the mouse path now calls `exceedsThreshold(dx, dy,
  thresholdPx)` and relies on `selection.ts`'s own `DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX` default, so
  the "@dnd-kit distance: 2" value lives in one place. The `thresholdPx` /
  `longPressMs` / `touchCancelSlopPx` options stay: the gesture tests vary them
  (bun:test has no fake timers, so the touch tests set `longPressMs: 1`).
- **[drag-to-create]**: Flattened `onPointerMove` by extracting `tryActivate`, so
  the handler is `if (!gesture.active && !tryActivate(...)) return` instead of a
  three-level `if` nest.
- **[calendar]**: Added a `data-calendar-scroll-content` contract test alongside
  the existing `data-calendar-viewport` / `data-start` ones.

## Notes

- The auto-scroll, mirror placement, and axis-lock depend on real layout
  (`getBoundingClientRect`, scroll offsets, stacking) that happy-dom can't model,
  so they need visual verification on the demo. The pure helpers (`computeEdgeScroll`,
  `unionRect`, `intersectRect`) are unit-tested; `orientation` on the public API is.
- Stacking relies on the mirror (`z-15`), cells (`z-10`), resource column
  (`z-20`), and header (`z-21`) sharing a stacking context. The mirror mounts into
  the same scroll-content box as the column, so the column directly outranks it;
  the header is a sibling of that box at `z-21` and outranks the whole subtree.

# Development Log - 2026-06-24

Source: https://github.com/kcsujeet/ilamy-calendar/blob/main/docs/logs/2026-06-24.md

# Development Log - 2026-06-24

## Changes

- **[ui/event-form]**: Added a `ColorPicker` (new `@ilamy/ui` primitive) to the
  event form: a Popover with the original 14 Tailwind class-pair swatches
  (theme-aware, rendered via their own className) PLUS a native
  `<input type="color">` + hex field for any custom color (no new dependency,
  built on Popover + Input). The stored value stays a class-pair when a swatch is
  picked (backward compatible); a custom pick stores `backgroundColor` (hex) +
  a `readableTextColor()`-derived `color`. Existing events are never rewritten
  unless the user actually picks a new color — editing other fields preserves the
  original color (legacy class-pair or hex) exactly.
- **[utils]**: Added `readableTextColor(hex)` to `@ilamy/utils/helpers`
  (YIQ perceived-brightness, W3C AERT formula) — picks black/white for contrast
  on custom hex colors.
- **[event-form]**: The Description field now renders a multi-line `Textarea`
  (via a `multiline` option on the shared `EventFormTextField`) instead of a
  single-line `Input` (also avoids the input autofill dropdown).
- **[ui]**: `ColorPicker` trigger derives a label from a Tailwind background
  class (`bg-cyan-100 ...` -> "Cyan") so colors outside the swatch set show their
  name instead of "Pick a color" (which now only shows when no color is set).

- **[calendar/header]**: Replaced the month/year/week/day title dropdowns in the
  header with `Select` instead of a `Popover` + list of `Button`s. Each picker is
  now a controlled `Select` whose options carry the `Dayjs` they navigate to;
  `onValueChange` looks the chosen option up and calls `selectDate`. The trigger
  keeps each view's distinct title format (e.g. the day picker's "Monday, 5") by
  rendering custom trigger content instead of `SelectValue`, with `aria-label`
  set to the title so the combobox has an accessible name.

- **[calendar/header]**: Fixed the day picker's "Today" badge layout. With the
  fixed `w-40` content the date ("Jun 24, 2026") wrapped and the badge got jammed
  in. The `SelectContent` now sizes to its widest item (`min-w-40`), items are
  `whitespace-nowrap`, and the badge is a proper pill (`px-1.5 py-0.5 leading-none`).

- **[demo/website]**: Added a CSS rule to both consumer global stylesheets so
  Radix popups (Select/Dialog/Popover) no longer hide the page scrollbar / shift
  layout on open. react-remove-scroll locks body scroll with
  `body[data-scroll-locked] { overflow: hidden !important; margin-right: <gap>px !important }`;
  the doubled `[data-scroll-locked][data-scroll-locked]` selector (specificity
  0,2,0 > the lib's 0,1,1) forces `overflow-y: scroll` + `margin-right: 0`. This
  affects every Radix Select in the app (recurrence editor, event form, settings,
  header), not just the header. See shadcn-ui/ui#4227.

- **[calendar/header]**: Stopped the header `Select` trigger from keeping a focus
  ring after closing. Radix returns focus to the trigger on close (via
  `FocusScope`), which left a `:focus-visible` ring until the next click;
  `onCloseAutoFocus={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` on the header `SelectContent`
  suppresses the focus-return. Scoped to the header (not the shared `SelectContent`).

## Files Modified

- `packages/ui/src/components/color-picker.tsx` - new `ColorPicker` primitive.
- `packages/utils/src/helpers.ts` - added `readableTextColor(hex)`.
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/event-form/event-form.tsx` -
  swapped the swatch buttons for `ColorPicker`; stores `backgroundColor` + derived
  `color`; legacy class-pair color constants removed.
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/event-form/event-form.test.tsx` -
  Color Selection tests rewritten for the picker (open trigger -> swatch ->
  assert `backgroundColor`/`color` on save).
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/header/title-content.tsx` -
  rewritten from Popover+Button to Select; options are plain data (string label +
  `today` flag), the "today" badge is rendered at the `SelectItem` level.
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/header/base-header.test.tsx` -
  the month-select test now drives `getByRole('combobox')` → `getByRole('option')`;
  the week-label test queries the trigger as `combobox`.
- `apps/demo/src/styles/globals.css`, `apps/website/src/styles/globals.css` -
  added the `[data-scroll-locked][data-scroll-locked]` scrollbar-preserve rule.
- `apps/website/src/content/docs/customization/styling.mdx` - documented the
  optional scrollbar-preserve CSS for consumers (framed as optional, links
  shadcn-ui/ui#4227).

## Notes

- The header `Select` triggers intentionally have no associated `<label>`, so the
  combobox accessible name comes from `aria-label` (set to the current title). The
  recurrence/event-form selects get their name from a `<Label htmlFor>` instead.
- Custom trigger content (not `SelectValue`) is what preserves the per-view title
  format; Radix Select doesn't require `Select.Value` for the trigger to function.
- Verified: 811 calendar tests pass, type-check clean, biome clean.

# Development Log - 2026-06-26

## Changes

- **[calendar/header]**: Full header redesign. Navigation (grouped prev/next,
  Today, and the title-as-dropdown) on the left; view + actions on the right.

    second row only when too narrow. The inner row is `justify-center` by
    default and `@lg/base-header:justify-between` once the compact row fits

    above, compact `ViewMenu` dropdown below. Export/New show their labels at
    `@2xl` and collapse to icon-only below. Both control variants live in the
    DOM (one `display:none`); in happy-dom the segmented radios and the Export
    button are the unique matches (menus stay closed), so tests are unambiguous.
- **[calendar/header]**: The title is a single context-aware date picker
  (`HeaderDatePicker`, an outline `Button` trigger so its border/height match
  the other header buttons): day/week open a day grid, month opens a Jan–Dec
  `MonthGrid` (year pager), year opens a `YearGrid` (12-year block pager). Week
  titles spanning two years drop the year (see use-date-time-formatters).

  **pure CSS** (no JS hover state):

    `group/week` + `group-hover/week:bg-accent` (rounded only at the row ends).
  - `highlightedWeekOf` statically marks the current week with a solid
    `bg-primary` bar (mirrors the day picker's selected day) and stays put while
    a different week is hovered.
  - "today" switched from a filled cell to an outline ring; width uses the
    `w-72` token (was an arbitrary `w-[280px]`); day-cell rendering extracted to
    `DayCell` + `dayButtonClass`/`cellClass`.

  calendar has resources (shared by switcher + menu).

  `default` size variant (token-only, no hand-picked `h-7`/`h-full`); the
  control totals `h-9` to match the action buttons.

  two years. `Intl.formatRange` otherwise injects the year on BOTH ends

  always spans two different months, so "Dec 30 – Jan 5" stays unambiguous.
  Same-year ranges keep `formatRange`'s concise collapsing.

# Development Log - 2026-06-28

Source: https://github.com/kcsujeet/ilamy-calendar/blob/main/docs/logs/2026-06-28.md

# Development Log - 2026-06-28

## Changes

- **[release]**: Cut v2.0.0 — the first release off the v2 overhaul (plugin-first architecture:
  opt-in recurrence, Agenda + drag-to-create plugins, unified `IlamyCalendar` with resources as
  props, `dayjs` peer dependency, custom views). Bumped `packages/calendar/package.json` to
  2.0.0 and added the CHANGELOG entry; breaking-changes section links the website migration
  guide (https://ilamy.dev/docs/help/migration-to-v2).

- **[header date picker] (refactor/generic-header-date-picker)**: Made the header title /
  date-picker plugin-agnostic. Core previously hardcoded agenda: a `view === 'agenda'` check, a
  `getAgendaPickerView()` that knew agenda's window semantics, and a reserved `agenda` title key
  in `header-date-picker.tsx`. A third-party view named anything else could only get the plain
  day picker. Replaced all of it with a generic `pickerKind(view)` that derives the picker form
  from the view's own navigation metadata (`navigationStep` / `navigationUnit`, the same fields
  that already drive prev/next): a single `day`/`week`/`month`/`year` step borrows that grid's
  picker + title; any other step (amount > 1, or a custom unit) shows the day picker over the
  view's `range`. Nothing in core references a view by name now. The agenda plugin and the four
  built-in views needed NO changes — agenda's existing window→navigationStep mapping flows
  through the generic path (its three title tests pass unchanged, which is the proof). Documented
  the picker-derivation on `PluginView.navigationStep`'s JSDoc so plugin authors discover it.

- **[vertical-grid] (merged to main, PR #226)**: Fixed a long-standing resource vertical-grid
  alignment bug where the header columns filled the viewport but the body columns shrank to
  their `min-w-20` floor (left-aligned, empty space on the right). Fix: add `*:w-max` to the
  ScrollArea viewport's child classes so the Radix viewport wrapper is definite-width.

- **[grid border frame / Approach G]**: Replaced per-cell grid borders with gap-based lines and
  a single calendar-body frame, theme-driven so it works with any Tailwind/shadcn theme.
  - Column/row separators are drawn by `gap-px bg-border` on the grid containers (vertical body,
    horizontal rows, headers, all-day); cells are opaque `bg-background` and carry no
    `border-r`/`border-b`/`border-r-0`/`border-r!`. Removed the `isLastColumn`/`isLastRow`/
    `isLastCol`/`isLastHour` edge-border patches.
  - Sub-hour slots keep a `border-b border-dashed` divider between sub-slots; the solid hour
    lines come from the column's `grid gap-px bg-border`.
  - The sticky left gutter/spacer draws its right separator with an opaque box-shadow
    (`STICKY_GUTTER_SHADOW`) so the line survives horizontal scroll (a flex gap would slide
    under the sticky column) without doubling against the translucent border.
  - Header/all-day bottom separators are centralized on the structural containers
    (`vertical-grid-header` and `vertical-grid-all-day` divs) so each line is drawn once.
  - Disabled (non-business-hours) cells use `DISABLED_CELL_CLASSNAME`, now an opaque
    `color-mix(in oklch, var(--background), var(--foreground) 3%)` shade instead of
    `bg-secondary`, so the grid lines stay visible on disabled cells in both light and dark
    (shadcn's `secondary` sits on the dark border lightness and hid them).

- **[tests]**: Rewrote the grid DOM-contract tests to the new invariants (gap-px separators,
  `color-mix` disabled cells, box-shadow gutter): `vertical-grid-col.test.tsx`,
  `all-day-row.test.tsx`, `horizontal-grid-row.test.tsx`, `views/week.test.tsx`,
  `views/day.test.tsx`, `ilamy-calendar.test.tsx`.

- **[playground]**: Made the demo mobile-responsive. The tall settings panel previously
  stacked above the calendar on small screens, pushing the calendar far down the page. On
  mobile (`< lg`) the settings now live behind a sticky "Calendar Settings" trigger that opens
  a scrollable dialog, so the calendar is full-width and immediately visible; at `lg` an inline
  sidebar takes over. The mobile/desktop switch is pure CSS (`lg:hidden` / `hidden lg:block`),
  no JS breakpoint hook. The settings form renders in both spots; the fields bind via
  `useController`, so the two instances safely share one form state, and `FormCheckbox` now
  derives its id from `useId` so the duplicate mount has no colliding label/control ids.

  Layout/width: the playground root is now `w-full` (always 100% width) instead of
  `container mx-auto`, so the max-width/centering constraint lives with the consumers (the demo
  app already wraps it in `container mx-auto`; added the same wrapper to the website's
  `demo.astro`, which previously had none). The horizontal-scroll-on-mobile root cause was the
  demo `body`: the Vite/Bun starter set it to `grid place-items-center`, and `place-items-center`
  implies `justify-items: center`, which sizes the grid item (`#root`) to its content width
  instead of stretching it to the viewport. So a wide calendar grew `#root` and scrolled the
  page. Fixed by dropping `grid place-items-center` from `body` (normal block flow → `#root`
  fills the viewport; the demo's `container mx-auto` already centers horizontally). Belt-and-
  suspenders: `#root` also carries `width: 100%` in `index.html`. Separately, `overflow-x-clip`
  on the playground root keeps a wide view (month/week columns have a `min-w-20` floor that can
  exceed a phone's width) from overflowing its container. `clip` (not `hidden`) is deliberate:
  per MDN `overflow: clip` is not a scroll container, so it does not hijack the calendar's sticky
  view header or the sticky settings trigger (which `overflow: hidden` would).

  Desktop sidebar width: switched the `lg` layout from a 4-col grid (settings `col-span-1`,
  calendar `col-span-3`) to `grid-cols-[20rem_minmax(0,1fr)]` — a fixed 20rem settings sidebar
  plus a flexible calendar column. The `col-span-1` quarter was too narrow even at ~1250px and
  truncated the segmented button groups (e.g. Agenda Window's "3-day"). `minmax(0,1fr)` lets the
  calendar column shrink instead of overflowing the grid.

- **[header]**: Fixed the toolbar flip-flopping between one and two rows at the same width
  when switching views. The row/stack decision now keys off the container width (`flex-col`
  below `@lg`, `flex-row` + `justify-between` at `@lg`+) instead of `flex-wrap`. `flex-wrap`
  keyed off content width, and the date title changes per view (`Jun 2026` vs
  `Jun 28 - Jul 4` vs `Sun, Jun 28, 2026`), which could tip a fixed-width container across the
  wrap threshold differently per view. The new layout is view-independent.

  settings dialog) switched by CSS, `overflow-x-clip` on the root.

  label/control id (the settings form mounts twice across breakpoints).
- `apps/website/src/pages/demo.astro` - wrapped the playground in `container mx-auto` so the
  website (a consumer) owns the width constraint now that the playground is `w-full`.
- `apps/demo/src/index.css` - dropped `grid place-items-center` from `body` so `#root` fills
  the viewport instead of shrink-wrapping to content (the cause of mobile horizontal scroll).
- `apps/demo/index.html` - `width: 100%` on `#root` (belt-and-suspenders for the above).
- `packages/calendar/src/features/calendar/components/views/{week,month,month-header,resource-axis,resource-week-vertical-day-header,resource-week-vertical-resource-header,resource-week-horizontal-day-header,time-header-row}.tsx`
  - gap-px headers/arrangements.
- Tests: `vertical-grid-col.test.tsx`, `all-day-row.test.tsx`, `horizontal-grid-row.test.tsx`,
  `views/week.test.tsx`, `views/day.test.tsx`, `ilamy-calendar.test.tsx`.

## Notes

### The `*:w-max` resource-vertical fix (root cause)

- Radix `ScrollArea` wraps the viewport content in an injected
  `<div style="min-width:100%; display:table">`. Our `viewPortProps` reshape it
  (`*:flex! *:flex-col! *:min-h-full`), but its width stays effectively **indefinite**.
- The vertical-grid **body** is `flex flex-1 min-w-full w-fit`. A non-sticky child sizing with a
  percentage (`min-w-full`) against an indefinite-width parent resolves to 0, so `w-fit`
  shrink-wraps the body to the sum of its columns' `min-w-20` minimums (columns never grow via
  `flex-1`).
- The **header** escapes this only because `VerticalGridHeaderContainer` is `position: sticky` —
  a sticky box resolves against the scroll viewport (definite), so its `min-w-full` resolves and
  columns fill. That asymmetry is why the header looked "longer" than the body despite both
  using `min-w-20` (a floor, not a target).
- `*:w-max` makes the wrapper definite (`width: max-content`) while `min-width:100%` keeps it
  >= the viewport: the body fills when narrow and still scrolls when wide.
- Debugging takeaway: when a flex/percentage child shrink-wraps inside a Radix ScrollArea,
  suspect the `display:table` viewport wrapper being width-indefinite. Sticky children mask it;
  non-sticky ones expose it (the wrapper measured ~524px while the sticky header filled).

### Why gap-px over per-cell borders

Translucent theme borders (e.g. dark `--border` at 10% white) double where a cell edge and the
body frame coincide. Drawing each line exactly once (gap reveals the container's `bg-border`,
cells occlude it) keeps lines uniform. `gap` was chosen over `divide-*` because `divide-*` would
add borders to every child including absolute events-layer overlays.

Verification: 826 calendar tests pass; type-check, Biome, full build, and the Fallow gate clean.

# Migrating to @ilamy/calendar v2

Source: https://github.com/kcsujeet/ilamy-calendar/blob/main/docs/migration-v2.md

# Migrating to @ilamy/calendar v2

v2 introduces a plugin architecture. The core is now plugin-agnostic; capabilities like recurring events are opt-in plugins. This guide covers every breaking change with before/after examples.

## 1. Plugins are opt-in — recurrence no longer works by default

In v1, recurring event expansion happened automatically. In v2 the core ships zero plugins. You must register `recurrencePlugin` explicitly.

**Before (v1)**

```tsx
import { IlamyCalendar } from '@ilamy/calendar'

// Recurring events expanded automatically
<IlamyCalendar events={events} />
```

**After (v2)**

```tsx
import { IlamyCalendar } from '@ilamy/calendar'
import { recurrencePlugin } from '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'

// Register the plugin to restore recurring-event behavior
<IlamyCalendar events={events} plugins={[recurrencePlugin()]} />
```

If you have no recurring events you can omit the plugin entirely and skip the `@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence` import.

## 2. Recurrence helpers moved to a subpath

`generateRecurringEvents`, `isRecurringEvent`, `RRule`, and `RRuleOptions` are no longer exported from the main `@ilamy/calendar` entry. Import them from the dedicated subpath.

**Before (v1)**

```ts
import {
  generateRecurringEvents,
  isRecurringEvent,
  RRule,
  type RRuleOptions,
} from '@ilamy/calendar'
```

**After (v2)**

```ts
import {
  generateRecurringEvents,
  isRecurringEvent,
  RRule,
  type RRuleOptions,
} from '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'
```

## 3. `CalendarEvent` no longer has recurrence fields by default

In v1, `CalendarEvent` declared `rrule`, `recurrenceId`, and `exdates` directly. In v2 those fields are not on the core type. They are re-added via TypeScript declaration merging when you import from `@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence`.

**Before (v1)**

```ts
// rrule, recurrenceId, exdates were always present on CalendarEvent
const event: CalendarEvent = {
  id: '1',
  title: 'Weekly standup',
  start: dayjs('2026-01-05T09:00:00Z'),
  end: dayjs('2026-01-05T09:30:00Z'),
  rrule: { freq: RRule.WEEKLY },
}
```

**After (v2)**

```ts
// Import the recurrence subpath first — this runs the declaration merge
import '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'
// or, more commonly, import recurrencePlugin (same effect)
import { recurrencePlugin } from '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'

// Now CalendarEvent has rrule / recurrenceId / exdates again
const event: CalendarEvent = {
  id: '1',
  title: 'Weekly standup',
  start: dayjs('2026-01-05T09:00:00Z'),
  end: dayjs('2026-01-05T09:30:00Z'),
  rrule: { freq: RRule.WEEKLY },
}
```

If TypeScript reports `Property 'rrule' does not exist on type 'CalendarEvent'`, make sure you are importing from `@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence` somewhere in your project.

## 4. Context method renames

The recurrence-specific context methods were replaced with generic plugin-routing equivalents. The public context type is now `IlamyCalendarApi` (was `UseIlamyCalendarContextReturn`).

| v1 method | v2 replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `updateRecurringEvent(event, updates, options)` | `applyScopedEdit(event, updates, scope)` | `scope` is opaque; gathered via the mutation-scope slot |
| `deleteRecurringEvent(event, options)` | `applyScopedDelete(event, scope)` | same |
| `findParentRecurringEvent(event)` | **removed** | moved into the recurrence plugin; use `rawEvents` to find the base series if needed |

**Before (v1)**

```ts
import { useIlamyCalendarContext } from '@ilamy/calendar'

const { updateRecurringEvent, deleteRecurringEvent } = useIlamyCalendarContext()

// Edit this and following
updateRecurringEvent(event, { title: 'New title' }, { scope: 'thisAndFollowing' })

// Delete just this occurrence
deleteRecurringEvent(event, { scope: 'this' })
```

**After (v2)**

```ts
import { useIlamyCalendarContext } from '@ilamy/calendar'

const { applyScopedEdit, applyScopedDelete } = useIlamyCalendarContext()

// The scope value is produced by the recurrence plugin's mutation-scope dialog
// and passed back automatically by useScopedEventMutation inside the host.
// Direct callers pass the opaque scope they received from the plugin:
applyScopedEdit(event, { title: 'New title' }, scope)
applyScopedDelete(event, scope)
```

In most applications you do not call `applyScopedEdit`/`applyScopedDelete` directly. The host's built-in scoped-mutation flow (driven by the event form and drag-and-drop) handles them automatically when the recurrence plugin is registered.

**`rawEvents` is now public.** If you previously relied on `findParentRecurringEvent` to locate the base rrule event of a generated instance, use `rawEvents` from `useIlamyCalendarContext()` and filter by `uid`:

```ts
const { rawEvents } = useIlamyCalendarContext()
const baseEvent = rawEvents.find(
  (e) => e.uid === instance.uid && e.rrule !== undefined
)
```

## 5. `CalendarView` is now `string`

In v1 `CalendarView` was a closed union (`'month' | 'week' | 'day' | 'year'`). In v2 it is `string` so plugins can register additional views.

**Before (v1)**

```ts
import type { CalendarView } from '@ilamy/calendar'

const view: CalendarView = 'week' // one of four literal values
```

**After (v2)**

```ts
import type { CalendarView } from '@ilamy/calendar'

const view: CalendarView = 'week' // still works — CalendarView is now string
```

Code that compares or switches on the built-in view names still works. The change only matters if you previously relied on exhaustive narrowing or type-level enforcement of exactly four views.

The built-in views are `'month'`, `'week'`, `'day'`, and `'year'` — themselves `PluginView` specs resolved through the same path as plugin views (see `docs/custom-views.md`).

## 6. Deep imports are blocked

The `exports` map in `package.json` now encapsulates the package. Any import path that is not listed in the map throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at runtime (and a TypeScript error at compile time).

**Before (v1)**

```ts
// Some projects imported internal modules directly
import { something } from '@ilamy/calendar/src/lib/utils'
import { CalendarContext } from '@ilamy/calendar/src/features/calendar/contexts/...'
```

**After (v2)**

These paths no longer work. The only valid entry points are:

```ts
import { ... } from '@ilamy/calendar'
import { ... } from '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'
```

Everything that was previously accessible via deep imports is either available from one of these two entries or was intentionally internal. If you find something you need that is missing, open an issue.

## 7. `dayjs` is now a peer dependency

`dayjs` moved from a bundled dependency to a **peer dependency** so your app and the calendar share a single `dayjs` instance. Previously, package managers (notably pnpm) could resolve a separate `dayjs` copy for `@ilamy/calendar`, so a locale you imported in your app (`import 'dayjs/locale/fr'`) registered onto your copy but not the calendar's, leaving some dates unlocalized.

Install `dayjs` explicitly (most apps already do, since `CalendarEvent.start`/`end` are `dayjs` objects):

```bash
npm install dayjs
```

With a shared instance, localizing dates is just importing the locale once in your app — no copying locale data between instances:

```ts
import 'dayjs/locale/fr'
// <IlamyCalendar locale="fr" />
```

If you previously worked around the split instance (e.g. reading `rootDayjs.Ls[locale]` and calling `dayjs.locale(data, undefined, true)` on the calendar's `dayjs`), you can delete that code.

## Type tightening (v2 structure overhaul, Phase 0)

### `Translations` is now a derived type alias, not an interface

`Translations` is now `Record<keyof typeof defaultTranslations, string>`. Annotating your
translation objects keeps working unchanged. The only break: `declare module` augmentation
that merged extra keys into the `Translations` interface no longer compiles — pass a
`translator` function for custom keys instead.

### `data` fields are `Record<string, unknown>` (was `Record<string, any>`)

Applies to `CalendarEvent.data` and `Resource.data`. Writing data is unchanged. Reads now
need narrowing:

**Before (v1)**

```ts
const role = resource.data.role
```

**After (v2)**

```ts
const role = typeof resource.data?.role === 'string' ? resource.data.role : undefined
```

Or cast once at your own boundary: `const meta = resource.data as MyResourceMeta`.

### `Resource.position` removed

The optional `position` field on `Resource` was never read by the calendar. Order resources
by ordering the `resources` array itself.

## Provider unification (v2 structure overhaul, Phase 2)

### Resource calendar: cell-click fallback now respects the cell's `allDay` flag

**Before (v1):** clicking a cell on `IlamyResourceCalendar` without a custom `onCellClick`
always pre-filled the event form with `allDay: false`, even for all-day cells.

**After (v2):** the pre-filled event respects the clicked cell's flag (`allDay: true` for
all-day cells), matching what `IlamyCalendar` has always done. If you depended on the old
hardcode, pass `onCellClick` and open the form yourself with the shape you want.

### `getEventsForResource` on `useIlamyCalendarContext()` works everywhere

In v1 it only existed at runtime on resource calendars while the type claimed it was
always present, so calling it on a regular calendar compiled and then crashed. Since the
resource axis moved into the one provider (Phase 4 below), it is genuinely always defined:
on a calendar without resources it simply filters by the events' own
`resourceIds`/`resourceId` fields. v1 call sites keep working unchanged.

### `PluginView` gains optional view-spec fields (non-breaking)

`PluginView` adds `navigationStep`, `range`, `columns`, `layout`, `renderHeader`, and
`supportsResources` — all optional. Existing view objects (`{ name, label, component,
navigationUnit }`) keep working unchanged; verified against the v1 plugin-view shape in the
test suite. New capability, not a break: a view that declares `columns` + `layout` renders
through the calendar's shared engines, `range` drives the event pipeline, and
`navigationStep` makes prev/next jump custom windows. See `docs/custom-views.md`.

One behavior change ships alongside (see "View switcher" below): on a **resource** calendar
the switcher now hides plugin views that don't declare `supportsResources: true`. They
previously showed a button that rendered a blank body.

### `PluginView.component` is now optional (non-breaking)

Spec-driven views (those declaring `columns` + `layout`) no longer need a dummy
`component: () => null` — omit the field entirely. Component-only views keep working
unchanged. A view that declares neither `columns`/`layout` nor `component` renders
nothing; dev builds log a console warning naming the view.

### Custom view spec types tightened

Only relevant if you author custom views (`PluginView.columns`):

- **`VerticalColumnSpec.resourceId` removed.** `resource` is the single carrier of the
  column's resource identity; the calendar derives the id from `resource.id`. Replace
  `{ resourceId: r.id, resource: r }` with `{ resource: r }`.
- **`HorizontalRowSpec.id` is now `string`** (was `string | number`), matching
  `VerticalColumnSpec.id`. Stringify numeric ids: `id: String(resource.id)`.
- **`PluginView.range`'s `config` parameter is now typed
  `Pick<ViewConfig, 'firstDayOfWeek'>`** — the only slice it ever received at runtime.
  Implementations annotated with the full `ViewConfig` still compile (the narrower
  argument is assignable); only code that read other fields off `range`'s config (they
  were always `undefined`) needs updating.

### View switcher: resource calendars hide resource-incapable plugin views

On `IlamyResourceCalendar`, plugin views now appear in the view switcher only if they
declare `supportsResources: true`. Previously every plugin view got a button that rendered
a blank body. Regular calendars list plugin views exactly as before. Plugin view `label`s
are now passed through the translator; unknown keys render verbatim, so plain-text labels
are unaffected.

### `applyEdit`/`applyDelete` may return a structured `PluginMutationResult` (additive, non-breaking)

Only relevant if you author a plugin that implements `applyEdit` or `applyDelete`. A scoped
mutation can change multiple stored rows at once (e.g. a recurring "this" edit adds an EXDATE
to the base row *and* creates a detached override; a recurring "all" delete drops the base
*and* every override). Returning a plain `CalendarEvent[]` forces the core to guess which
persistence callback to fire, so it always fired one `onEventUpdate` (edit) or one
`onEventDelete` for the clicked event (delete) — the wrong payload and, for multi-row
mutations, the wrong count.

Both `applyEdit` and `applyDelete` widened their return type from `CalendarEvent[]` to
`CalendarEvent[] | PluginMutationResult`:

```ts
export interface PluginMutationResult {
  events: CalendarEvent[]   // the full next event list (replaces the store)
  updated: CalendarEvent[]  // existing rows to persist via onEventUpdate
  added: CalendarEvent[]    // new rows to persist via onEventAdd
  deleted: CalendarEvent[]  // existing rows to persist via onEventDelete
}
```

When you return a `PluginMutationResult`, the core dispatches each `updated` row to
`onEventUpdate`, each `added` row to `onEventAdd`, each `deleted` row to `onEventDelete`, and
sets the store to `events` — the real stored rows, with their own ids/uids. Returning a bare
`CalendarEvent[]` behaves exactly as before (one synthetic callback, store replaced), so
existing plugins compile and run unchanged. The built-in recurrence plugin now returns the
structured result from both hooks.

**Behavior change for scoped recurring deletes.** They now report the actual stored rows
removed or updated rather than a single `onEventDelete` for the clicked instance:

- delete "this" fires `onEventUpdate` for the base event's new EXDATE (and `onEventDelete`
  for the dropped override, if one existed) — not `onEventDelete` for a generated instance
  that was never stored.
- delete "all" fires `onEventDelete` once per stored row in the series (the base plus every
  detached override).
- delete "following" fires `onEventUpdate` for the terminated base.

Likewise, an edit-"all" reset now fires `onEventDelete` for each detached override it drops.
If you persist per-row to an external store, these callbacks keep it consistent; previously
the dropped rows were silently left behind as stale data.

PR #194 also addresses issue #156: scoped recurring DELETE now reports the real stored rows
(this/following → base `onEventUpdate`, all → base `onEventDelete`), and the fired payload
always carries the base event's id, never a generated `<id>_0` instance id.

## One calendar: resources are props on `IlamyCalendar` (v2 structure overhaul, Phase 4)

`IlamyCalendar` now accepts `resources`, `renderResource`, `orientation`, and
`weekViewGranularity` directly. Behavior with resources set is unchanged: events render
per matching resource (`resourceIds`, falling back to `resourceId`), unassigned events
are hidden, visible hours are the union of global and per-resource business hours, and
the year view is hidden from the switcher.

**Before (v1)**

```tsx
<IlamyResourceCalendar resources={rooms} orientation="vertical" events={events} />
```

**After (v2)**

```tsx
<IlamyCalendar resources={rooms} orientation="vertical" events={events} />
```

`IlamyResourceCalendar` still works as a deprecated alias and will be removed in the
next major.

Other notes:

- `orientation` without `resources` is inert; dev builds now log a console warning.
- `IlamyResourceCalendarPropEvent` is gone — use `IlamyCalendarPropEvent`:
  `CalendarEvent` (and therefore the `events` prop) already carries
  `resourceId` / `resourceIds`.
- The root testid of a resource calendar is now `ilamy-calendar`
  (was `ilamy-resource-calendar`).
- The vertical-arrangement resource header testid is now `resource-columns-header`
  (was `resource-month-header` — the header serves the day AND month views).
- Forcing a resource-incapable view programmatically (e.g. `initialView="year"` with
  `resources`) renders it as a regular, resource-less view; the switcher still hides it.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Add `import { recurrencePlugin } from '@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence'` and pass `plugins={[recurrencePlugin()]}` to `<IlamyCalendar>` / `<IlamyResourceCalendar>`.
- [ ] Move any `generateRecurringEvents`, `isRecurringEvent`, `RRule`, `RRuleOptions` imports to `@ilamy/calendar/plugins/recurrence`.
- [ ] If TypeScript reports missing `rrule`/`recurrenceId`/`exdates`, ensure the recurrence subpath is imported somewhere in your project.
- [ ] Replace `updateRecurringEvent` calls with `applyScopedEdit` and `deleteRecurringEvent` calls with `applyScopedDelete`.
- [ ] Remove any calls to `findParentRecurringEvent`; use `rawEvents` filtering instead if needed.
- [ ] Remove any deep `@ilamy/calendar/src/...` imports; use only the two public entry points.
- [ ] Install `dayjs` as a direct dependency (it is now a peer dependency). Remove any workaround that synced locale data between a separate app `dayjs` copy and the calendar's.
- [ ] If you have TypeScript code that narrows `CalendarView` as an exhaustive union, update it for the new `string` type.
- [ ] If you read properties off `event.data` / `resource.data`, add narrowing or a boundary cast (`Record<string, unknown>` now).
- [ ] Remove any use of `Resource.position`; order the `resources` array instead.
- [ ] Resource calendars: if you relied on cell-click always creating `allDay: false` events, handle it in `onCellClick`.
- [ ] Replace `<IlamyResourceCalendar>` with `<IlamyCalendar resources={...}>` (the old name still works as a deprecated alias).
- [ ] If your test harness queried the `ilamy-resource-calendar` root testid, query `ilamy-calendar` instead.
- [ ] If your test harness queried the `resource-month-header` testid, query `resource-columns-header` instead.
- [ ] Custom view authors: drop `component: () => null` from spec-driven views, replace `resourceId` with `resource` on `VerticalColumnSpec`, and stringify numeric `HorizontalRowSpec.id`s.
